subject: Request: access scope attestations for telemetry & support providers (SIG follow-up)
messages:
From: CloudBridge Solutions <security@cloudbridge.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: attestations for telemetry & support providers

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for taking the SIG — quick follow-up. Our assessor has asked for a short, auditable list of the specific access scopes that each of your telemetry and support vendors hold. Specifically:
- Which vendors have log/store access to production request/response telemetry (even if redacted)?
- Which vendors can access customer-identifying metadata?
- Which vendors have the ability to run queries or exports of telemetry?

If you can provide a compact spreadsheet mapping vendor -> minimal access level + the most recent attestation date, that will keep us moving. I attached an example template and the evidence intake instructions.

We can accept S3/object-store permissions screenshots, scoped IAM roles, or a signed attestation. If you already have a prior SIG clause or subprocessor doc we can reference, please send that too.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20‑minute call if easier.

— Priya S.
Security Team | CloudBridge Solutions
security@cloudbridge.com

Attachments: cloudbridge_evidence_instructions.pdf
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: CloudBridge Solutions <security@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-17T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: attestations for telemetry & support providers

Hi Priya — thanks for the clarity. We're compiling that now. A couple of quick notes up front so the assessor has context:

- Redwood separates 'telemetry' (production token/usage metrics, traces, aggregated latency stats) from 'payload' (customer prompts/responses). Our default policy is telemetry-only vendors do not have access to decrypted payload.
- For support tooling, agents can see account identifiers and case notes if the customer has given consent via support flow; by default we mask user content in support transcripts.

I'll upload a spreadsheet mapping each vendor to the minimal access level (none / metrics-only / metadata-only / logs-export / full) and the last attestation. Vivek will pull the IAM role screenshots for cloud providers where applicable.

Timeline: we can deliver the spreadsheet + attachments by Tuesday EOD Pacific (2027-04-20) unless you need it sooner.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Manager, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_min_access_v1.xlsx (draft)

Forwarding internal pull together & initial evidence plan.

On Fri, Apr 17, 2027 at 10:04 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Priya — thanks for the clarity. We're compiling that now. A couple of quick notes up front...

Team — I exported the access mapping from our internal asset inventory and started filling the spreadsheet Monica attached. Quick summary of where we are:
- Cloud infra: AWS (prod account) — we will provide IAM role names + last rotated keys screenshots. Permissions are restricted (CloudWatch readonly, S3 telemetry-bucket read for analytics-role).
- Telemetry pipeline: Datadog — metrics-only, tracing sampling enabled; engineers do not have access to PII. We'll include a scoped org role screenshot and the service account binding.
- Support: Zendesk — agents have access to account identifiers and support transcripts; transcript masking is enabled by default for payload. We'll export the role configuration and a sample (redacted) transcript.

I'll attach the screenshots and a short note describing RBAC controls. If CloudBridge needs signed attestations instead of screenshots, flag that and we'll obtain sign-off from Legal.

— Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Security
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

If you can include the sample redacted transcript from Zendesk and an explicit line in the spreadsheet that says 'no access to raw customer payload' for telemetry vendors, that will close a number of open questions.

If you can get the packet to us by Tuesday EOD Pacific, we'll slot the review into next Wednesday's assessor window.

— Priya
CloudBridge Security

Priya — attached is the completed mapping and the evidence bundle per your guidance. Highlights:
- Telemetry vendors: Datadog (metrics-only), Lightstep (sampled traces, metadata-only), S3 backups (encrypted, logs-only)

- Cloud infra: AWS prod (scoped IAM roles listed), GCP logging ingest (write-only service account)
